groups.text: It is currently 21 degrees and cloudy in Berlin-Tempelhof.
With the morning weather set, here is the news.

Wall Street is pricing in fast earnings growth from artificial intelligence, but real cash flows may trail far behind. Torsten Slok, the chief economist at Apollo, warns that profit gains outside the tech sector could take well beyond what investors currently expect. In regulated industries like banking, healthcare, pharma, energy, and manufacturing, privacy requirements and process overhauls could delay productivity boosts by years. This creates a significant risk for AI company valuations, which rely on rising margins across the S&P 493. Slok notes that if these gains take five years instead of five months, many stocks face a painful repricing. Furthermore, measuring productivity in knowledge work remains difficult. Without clear metrics, management cannot act on improvements, meaning any efficiency gains are simply absorbed into daily operations rather than appearing on the balance sheet.

Ukraine is intensifying its long-range attacks to trigger a domestic fuel supply crisis within Russia. Robert Brovdi, the top drone warfare commander known as Madyar, reports that overnight aerial strikes in the Sea of Azov achieved industrial-scale results. He claims Ukrainian drones hit a convoy of eight Russian shadow fleet tankers, leaving them badly damaged and on fire. The operation also targeted a ferry and a dry cargo ship. Brovdi says these strikes are part of an ongoing battle for fuel destined for Crimea, noting that the shadow fleet is now leaving the area. These naval attacks coincide with strikes on power plants and logistics in occupied Crimea, which have disrupted local power. While Moscow has not yet commented and the claims remain independently unverified, the operation marks a significant escalation in Ukraine's effort to sever Russian energy logistics.

Severe weather is claiming lives across several regions of China. In Hubei province, a tornado has left at least eleven people dead and hundreds injured, while an earthquake-like landslide in Gansu province killed five more. President Xi Jinping has ordered all available forces to mobilize for rescue efforts. This follows a dam breach at the Liulan reservoir in Guangxi that flooded an entire region and displaced tens of thousands of residents. Now, Super Typhoon Bavi is moving toward the coast. In other news, Italian energy contractor Saipem has secured a two-billion-dollar contract to build a floating production storage and offloading unit for Eni’s Kutei North Hub project in Indonesia. Meanwhile, in Marseille, French authorities have jailed four more suspects for the organized gang murder of Mehdi Kessaci. The victim was the brother of Amine Kessaci, an environmental activist known for fighting drug trafficking.

Ukrainian drones have struck the Omsk Oil Refinery in Western Siberia, causing a major fire and damaging critical installations. President Volodymyr Zelenskyy declared that Siberia is now within reach, signaling an expansion of Ukraine's long-range strike capabilities to weaken Russia's economic and military logistics. This escalation contrasts with shifts in European financial policy, where the European Central Bank will begin penalizing corporate bonds from climate-vulnerable sectors in 2026. The ECB is introducing a climate factor that applies additional haircuts to these bonds when used as collateral, effectively pricing transition risk into monetary operations. Meanwhile, in the world of esports, League of Legends powerhouse T1 is utilizing hidden draft strategies at MSI 2026. Jungler Mun “Oner” Hyeon-jun confirmed the team has reserved champion picks for higher-stakes matches, a move that impacts crypto-native prediction markets tracking tournament outcomes.

French data protection regulator CNIL has issued twenty-three sanctions since January using its simplified procedure, with nineteen of those cases stemming from formal complaints. The agency targeted companies in fast food, urban transport, and railway station commerce for filming employees or operating video devices without prefectural authorization. Other penalties focused on the illegal use of third-party cookies and incomplete information banners, specifically affecting online ticket sellers and telemarketing firms. In a separate shift for software users, Mozilla is scrapping its Thunderbird Pro branding to resolve confusion over whether the classic application would become a paid product. Following community feedback that prioritized webmail over other bundled services like Appointment and Sens, the foundation is replacing the Pro label with Thundermail. This new name will cover all paid offerings, while the Thunderbird name remains reserved exclusively for the desktop and mobile versions of the app.

Developers are working to stabilize local AI performance with the release of llama.cpp version b9895. This update focuses on critical memory safety, specifically introducing speculative fixes for out-of-bounds reads in the ngram-map during prompt shrink operations. These patches also address cleanup cutoffs following a prompt shrink to prevent system instability. The release expands hardware compatibility across several platforms. It supports macOS Apple Silicon with KleidiAI enabled and various Linux distributions including Ubuntu on x64 and arm64 architectures using Vulkan, ROCm 7.2, and OpenVINO. Windows users gain support for CUDA versions 12.4 and 13.3, alongside SYCL and HIP. The update also extends to Android arm64 and openEuler systems utilizing the 310p and 910b ACL Graph. By refining how these models handle prompt shrinking across diverse chipsets, the project aims to reduce crashes for users running large language models on their own hardware.

German factory output rose more than expected in May, with industrial, construction, and energy production increasing by 0.9 percent. This growth was driven largely by a 3.6 percent jump in car production, though recovery remains fragile. Energy-intensive sectors edged up 0.2 percent despite pressure from higher costs linked to the Iran conflict. In other news, German breweries are seeing non-alcoholic beer move into the mainstream, with output worth nearly 700 million euros in 2025. This shift in consumer taste contrasts with a legal battle over state security. Germany's Federal Constitutional Court is currently reviewing a Bavarian law that allows police to intervene before a concrete threat has emerged. These separate trends highlight a moment of economic stabilization alongside shifting social habits and ongoing debates over the limits of police power.
After the headlines, back to the weather.
This afternoon will be cloudy with temperatures between 18 and 22 degrees.
And from the weather, a quick look at the calendar.
On your calendar today: personal calendar: at 12:00, Weekly Lunch, at 12:45, Monthly Birthday Celebration, at 15:00, RAYX Meeting, and at 18:00, Krebs at c-base.
And that's it for your personal morning broadcast.
[mature adult voice, intensely emotional, tender, radiant; hold a long breath after Rise] Rise... and shine.
[very very long pause before speaking; then mature adult voice, most emotional, strong, warm, radiant, deeply encouraging; hold a long breath after Rise] Rise... and shine.
